candidate.title: OS-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina OS-Seq (oligonucleotide-selective sequencing) schematic: preparation of a single adaptor sample-DNA library in parallel with target-specific programming of flow-cell primers, convergence through target capture on the flow cell, extension/denaturation, bridge hybridization and extension/denaturation, and sequence reads 1 and 2. The Gene icon is descriptive context, not a separate gene-excision operation. No alternative target workflow is depicted. The matching collection page is secondary evidence; the supplied Hopmans abstract supports the central flow-cell capture architecture, without establishing every unshown implementation detail or equivalence among OS-Seq versions.

method_scopes.rationale: OS-Seq is the only target identified by the assigned card, image annotation, and matching collection heading/caption. All eight local operations belong to this schematic. The upper library path and lower surface-programming path are distinct preparations, converging at o_capture. Oligonucleotide-selective sequencing is the expanded name, not another method. The primary Hopmans abstract identifies in situ flow-cell modification, genomic capture, and sequencing as OS-Seq; the detailed route remains diagram-level evidence. Neither the unshown clinical panels nor the mistakenly listed Duplex Sequencing and psychiatric-survey references expand scope. The collection page additionally cites Myllykangas et al. (2011), linked to OS-Seq by footnote 124, and an Akinrinade et al. (2015) OS-Seq clinical application. These are catalogue-only associations: neither primary text nor independently verified metadata for them is present in the supplied registry, so they supply no primary chemistry or historical-priority evidence.
